merits: Three sections, all landscape A4 (16838x11906, orient=landscape): s0 single-column title page (cols num=1), s1 two-column verse body (cols num=2, equalWidth), s2 single-column colophon; render shows poems flowing side by side on page 2
Title (Title style, centered), subtitle, italic editor's note, frontispiece image (img0, 3.54x2.76in, with alt text) and italic 'Frontispiece' caption all on page 1
All four poems present with Heading1 titles (Preludes (I), The Hollow Men, Prufrock excerpt, The Waste Land opening); verse lines preserved as real line breaks, stanza gaps kept
Two footnotes with substantive editor's annotations (fn1 on 'Michelangelo' in Prufrock, fn2 on The Waste Land's April), rendered at the foot of page 2
Colophon hyperlink link0 'public domain' -> https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1321, rendered blue/underlined
Header 'A T. S. Eliot Reader' on every page; centered footer uses real PAGE/NUMPAGES fields and renders 'Page 1 of 3' / 'Page 2 of 3' / 'Page 3 of 3'
Garamond is the docDefaults face (read shows <!-- docx:base font="Garamond" -->) and the render shows serif in body, Title, Subtitle and headings; theme bindings cleared so Word honors it
No blank pages, no leftover placeholder/probe paragraphs; everything survives docx read, footnotes/hyperlinks/headers/footers/images list

defects.what: Footnote reference marks in the body render at baseline ('Michelangelo.1', 'tubers.2') instead of superscript: runs carry rStyle FootnoteReference but styles.xml defines only Normal/Title/Subtitle/Heading1, so the style is dangling
defects.evidence: page-002.png shows 'Talking of Michelangelo.1' and 'dried tubers.2' at text baseline; grep of word/styles.xml finds no w:styleId="FootnoteReference"

defects.what: Each poem's verse is one paragraph with <w:br/> line breaks rather than one paragraph per verse line; the rubric wording prefers separate paragraphs, though the task's 'each line on its own line' is met visually and in read
defects.evidence: read.md: whole Preludes stanza block is p7, Hollow Men is p9, etc.

notes: docx-cli's footers list/read reports the footer as 'Page 1 of 1' (cached field results) rather than {page}/{pages} tokens; the XML holds proper PAGE and NUMPAGES complex fields and Word renders them correctly, so this is a docx-cli reader limitation, not an OfficeCLI defect. Section 1 (verse) has no own header/footer references and inherits from s0 correctly. Agent's self-reported 'partial' was overly cautious; output meets every rubric item.
weakAgentStruggle: Moderate slog. The agent hit several silent traps: section breaks inserted via 'add --type section' gave the earlier section portrait size and no columns (needed separate set calls); header/footer 'add' attached only to the final sectPr (fixed with raw-set prepend on the first sectPr); setting style fonts left asciiTheme/hAnsiTheme overriding Garamond (fixed only by an undocumented empty-value set); batch JSON did not decode \v like --prop (verse rewritten with a real \u000b); 'Page X of Y' took four add calls; view issues false-flagged verse. It also created and later removed probe paragraphs. Each trap was silent and required OOXML knowledge to detect, which a weaker run could easily miss.
